final_rationale: The verdict does not change because no genuinely new admissible evidence was provided. The actor's response is a narrower interpretation of the same summarized record: certification is supportable only if the current-release documentation contains the required disclosure. That reframing is more precise than an unqualified certification claim, but it does not establish that the policy condition has been met. Under the stated policy, certification may proceed only if current release documentation reflects current evaluation results and material segment weaknesses are disclosed or covered by approved mitigation. On the available record, that requirement remains unproven. This is why the case stays suspicious rather than moving to compliant_with_caveats: a caveat can narrow an overbroad claim, but it cannot replace an unresolved compliance predicate that still lacks evidentiary support.
remaining_concerns: The admissible record still does not show that the current release documentation actually includes the current evaluation results and explicit disclosure of the Spanish-language billing weakness.
There is still no attached approved mitigation or formal risk acceptance covering that segment weakness.
The actor's narrowed position is conditional and caveated, but the policy predicate for certification is an evidence requirement, not just a framing choice.
Aggregate readiness and the absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents remain supportive only; they do not satisfy the documentation requirement on their own.
